# Psalm 103 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Of David. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name!

**2** Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits,

**3** who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,

**4** who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with steadfast love and mercy,

**5** who satisfies you with good so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.

**6** The LORD works righteousness and justice for all who are oppressed.

**7** He made known his ways to Moses, his acts to the people of Israel.

**8** The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.

**9** He will not always chide, nor will he keep his anger forever.

**10** He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities.

**11** For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him;

**12** as far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us.

**13** As a father shows compassion to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who fear him.

**14** For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust.

**15** As for man, his days are like grass; he flourishes like a flower of the field;

**16** for the wind passes over it, and it is gone, and its place knows it no more.

**17** But the steadfast love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness to children's children,

**18** to those who keep his covenant and remember to do his commandments.

**19** The LORD has established his throne in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all.

**20** Bless the LORD, O you his angels, you mighty ones who do his word, obeying the voice of his word!

**21** Bless the LORD, all his hosts, his ministers, who do his will!

**22** Bless the LORD, all his works, in all places of his dominion. Bless the LORD, O my soul!

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 103.

- **103:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **103:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **103:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **103:8**: Direct quotation of Exodus 34:6 — the foundational divine self-revelation. This verse is the theological center of the psalm.
- **103:12**: 'As-far-as east from west' — infinite distance (east and west never meet); the most vivid OT image of total forgiveness.
- **103:14**: 'Remembering that dust we-are' — echoes Genesis 2:7; God's compassion is grounded in knowing our fragility.

### LOGOS
- **103:1-5**: Five benefits listed in rapid succession: forgiveness, healing, redemption, love, satisfaction. The psalm is a catalogue of grace.
- **103:11-13**: Three analogies for God's love: as high as heaven (v. 11), as far as east from west (v. 12), as tender as a father (v. 13). Each approaches the same reality from a different angle.

### PNEUMA
- **103:10-12**: These might be the three most comforting verses in the entire Bible. He doesn't treat us as our sins deserve. He removes them as far as east is from west — which is an infinite distance. That's not just forgiveness; it's complete erasure.
- **103:14**: 'He remembers that we are dust.' This changes everything. God isn't disappointed that we're weak — he already knows. His expectations are calibrated to our reality, and his compassion flows from that knowledge.

— SOPHIA
